---- MODULE W4Od18m7p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Phones, Channels, MaxAllowance, NoRead, NoChannel

\* readOn/readVal are the phone's outstanding read: which channel's register it
\* looked at, and the number it saw. The room check is made against that number.
VARIABLES reg, readOn, readVal, session, allowance

vars == << reg, readOn, readVal, session, allowance >>

Carrying(ch) == Cardinality({p \in Phones : session[p] = ch})

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Channels -> 0..MaxAllowance]
    /\ readOn \in [Phones -> Channels \cup {NoChannel}]
    /\ readVal \in [Phones -> (0..MaxAllowance) \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ session \in [Phones -> Channels \cup {NoChannel}]
    /\ allowance \in [Channels -> 0..MaxAllowance]

Init ==
    /\ reg = [ch \in Channels |-> 0]
    /\ readOn = [p \in Phones |-> NoChannel]
    /\ readVal = [p \in Phones |-> NoRead]
    /\ session = [p \in Phones |-> NoChannel]
    /\ allowance = [ch \in Channels |-> 1]

ReadRegister(p, ch) ==
    /\ session[p] = NoChannel
    /\ readOn[p] = NoChannel
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![p] = ch]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![p] = reg[ch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, session, allowance >>

\* The compare half: a register that moved under the phone invalidates the
\* room judgement the phone made from its read.
Claim(p) ==
    /\ session[p] = NoChannel
    /\ readOn[p] # NoChannel
    /\ readVal[p] = reg[readOn[p]]
    /\ readVal[p] < allowance[readOn[p]]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![readOn[p]] = readVal[p] + 1]
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![p] = readOn[p]]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![p] = NoChannel]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![p] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << allowance >>

StaleRead(p) ==
    /\ readOn[p] # NoChannel
    /\ readVal[p] # reg[readOn[p]]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![p] = NoChannel]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![p] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, session, allowance >>

Release(p) ==
    /\ session[p] # NoChannel
    /\ reg[session[p]] > 0
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![session[p]] = @ - 1]
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![p] = NoChannel]
    /\ UNCHANGED << readOn, readVal, allowance >>

Reprovision(ch, n) ==
    /\ n # allowance[ch]
    /\ n >= reg[ch]
    /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![ch] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, readOn, readVal, session >>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Phones, ch \in Channels : ReadRegister(p, ch)
    \/ \E p \in Phones : Claim(p) \/ StaleRead(p) \/ Release(p)
    \/ \E ch \in Channels, n \in 0..MaxAllowance : Reprovision(ch, n)

\* Nothing blocks a release, so weak fairness per phone is enough.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A p \in Phones :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Release(p))

ChannelCarriesWithinAllowance ==
    \A ch \in Channels : Carrying(ch) <= allowance[ch]

EverySessionIsReleased ==
    \A p \in Phones : (session[p] # NoChannel) ~> (session[p] = NoChannel)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Phones = {phX, phY, phZ}
    Channels = {chLow, chHigh}
    MaxAllowance = 2
    NoRead = noRead
    NoChannel = noChannel

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ChannelCarriesWithinAllowance

PROPERTY EverySessionIsReleased
nl:
A smart-home hub carries unlock sessions on several radio channels. For each channel the hub keeps a single register holding how many sessions that channel is carrying, and phones contend for those registers directly: a phone reads a channel's register, then writes back its own read plus one only if the register still holds exactly what it read. Each channel has its own allowance, and the installer re-provisions a channel's allowance at runtime as the mesh grows or as interference forces the hub off a band, though never below what that channel is already carrying. Whether there is room is judged against the number the phone read, which is exactly why the write has to re-check.

A phone that holds no session and no outstanding read may read the register of any channel, remembering both the channel and the number it saw. A phone whose read still matches that channel's register, and whose read was below that channel's allowance, may claim a session on it: the register becomes its read plus one, the phone is on that channel, and its read is cleared. A phone whose remembered number no longer matches the register of the channel it read discards the read and will read again. A phone holding a session may release it, which lowers that channel's register by one. The installer may re-provision any channel's allowance to a different value that is not below the sessions that channel is already carrying.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every radio channel, the number of phones holding a session on that channel never exceeds that channel's currently provisioned allowance.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every phone that is holding an unlock session eventually releases it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m4p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cars, WashSlots, MaxDepth, NoSlot, NoCar

\* The office keeps both directions of the allocation; the safety property is
\* that they never disagree.
VARIABLES lane, slotOf, occupant, depth

vars == << lane, slotOf, occupant, depth >>

InLane(c) == \E i \in 1..Len(lane) : lane[i] = c

TypeOK ==
    /\ lane \in Seq(Cars)
    /\ Len(lane) <= MaxDepth
    /\ slotOf \in [Cars -> WashSlots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ occupant \in [WashSlots -> Cars \cup {NoCar}]
    /\ depth \in 0..MaxDepth

Init ==
    /\ lane = << >>
    /\ slotOf = [c \in Cars |-> NoSlot]
    /\ occupant = [s \in WashSlots |-> NoCar]
    /\ depth = 1

\* Backpressure: the lane refuses the car rather than growing past its depth.
JoinLane(c) ==
    /\ ~InLane(c)
    /\ slotOf[c] = NoSlot
    /\ Len(lane) < depth
    /\ lane' = Append(lane, c)
    /\ UNCHANGED << slotOf, occupant, depth >>

PutOnSlot(s) ==
    /\ Len(lane) > 0
    /\ occupant[s] = NoCar
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![Head(lane)] = s]
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = Head(lane)]
    /\ lane' = Tail(lane)
    /\ UNCHANGED << depth >>

DriveOff(c) ==
    /\ slotOf[c] # NoSlot
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![slotOf[c]] = NoCar]
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED << lane, depth >>

\* The depth moves during the day but never below what is already queued.
SetDepth(d) ==
    /\ d # depth
    /\ d >= Len(lane)
    /\ depth' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED << lane, slotOf, occupant >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : JoinLane(c) \/ DriveOff(c)
    \/ \E s \in WashSlots : PutOnSlot(s)
    \/ \E d \in 0..MaxDepth : SetDepth(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SlotRecordsAgree ==
    \A c \in Cars : slotOf[c] # NoSlot => occupant[slotOf[c]] = c

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carP, carQ, carR}
    WashSlots = {wash1, wash2}
    MaxDepth = 2
    NoSlot = noSlot
    NoCar = noCar

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SlotRecordsAgree
nl:
A car wash runs a conveyor with a small number of wash slots and a holding lane in front of it. The holding lane is a queue with backpressure: it has a depth, and while it is at depth the attendant turns cars away rather than letting them join. The depth is not fixed -- the site manager changes it during the day as the forecourt fills or empties, but never below the number of cars already waiting. Each car on the conveyor occupies exactly one slot, and the office keeps two records that must agree: which slot each car was put in, and which car each slot is holding.

A car that is not in the holding lane and not on the conveyor may join the back of the holding lane, provided the lane is below its current depth. The car at the front of the holding lane may be put onto any slot that is holding no car: it leaves the lane, the office records that slot against the car, and records the car against that slot. A car on the conveyor may drive off at the end of the wash, which clears both records. The site manager may set the lane depth to any different value that is not below the number of cars waiting in the lane.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every car the office has recorded against a wash slot, that slot's record names that same car, so no slot is ever recorded as holding two different cars.

---- MODULE W4Od1m4p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Flights, Runways, QueueDepth, MaxCancels, NoRunway

\* Each queue is a sequence: flights leave from the front, in order, and the
\* supervisor's cancellation is the only way out of the middle.
VARIABLES queue, phase, closed, cancels

vars == << queue, phase, closed, cancels >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in [Runways -> Seq(Flights)]
    /\ \A r \in Runways : Len(queue[r]) <= QueueDepth
    /\ phase \in [Flights -> {"gate", "queued", "airborne"}]
    /\ closed \in Runways \cup {NoRunway}
    /\ cancels \in 0..MaxCancels

Init ==
    /\ queue = [r \in Runways |-> << >>]
    /\ phase = [f \in Flights |-> "gate"]
    /\ closed = NoRunway
    /\ cancels = 0

\* Backpressure: the flight is held at the gate rather than the queue growing.
JoinQueue(f, r) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "gate"
    /\ Len(queue[r]) < QueueDepth
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![r] = Append(@, f)]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << closed, cancels >>

Launch(r, f) ==
    /\ r # closed
    /\ Len(queue[r]) > 0
    /\ Head(queue[r]) = f
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![r] = Tail(@)]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "airborne"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << closed, cancels >>

ReturnToGate(f) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "airborne"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "gate"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << queue, closed, cancels >>

\* The supervisor's cancellation reaches into the middle of a queue; the
\* flights behind it close up, so the queue only ever gets shorter.
Cancel(r, i) ==
    /\ i \in 1..Len(queue[r])
    /\ cancels < MaxCancels
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![queue[r][i]] = "gate"]
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![r] =
                   SubSeq(@, 1, i - 1) \o SubSeq(@, i + 1, Len(@))]
    /\ cancels' = cancels + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << closed >>

CloseRunway(r) == /\ closed = NoRunway /\ closed' = r /\ UNCHANGED << queue, phase, cancels >>
Reopen         == /\ closed # NoRunway /\ closed' = NoRunway /\ UNCHANGED << queue, phase, cancels >>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : JoinQueue(f, r) \/ Launch(r, f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : ReturnToGate(f)
    \/ \E r \in Runways, i \in 1..QueueDepth : Cancel(r, i)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : CloseRunway(r)
    \/ Reopen

\* A cancelled flight goes back to the gate, so a flight needs a fair chance
\* to rejoin as well as to launch; its launch is only enabled once it reaches
\* the front of an open runway, hence strong fairness on both.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A f \in Flights :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E r \in Runways : JoinQueue(f, r))
        /\ SF_vars(\E r \in Runways : Launch(r, f))
    /\ WF_vars(Reopen)

QueuesRespectTheirDepth ==
    \A r \in Runways : Len(queue[r]) <= QueueDepth

EveryQueuedFlightLaunches ==
    \A f \in Flights : (phase[f] = "queued") ~> (phase[f] = "airborne")

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Flights = {flt1, flt2, flt3}
    Runways = {rwyL, rwyR}
    QueueDepth = 2
    MaxCancels = 1
    NoRunway = noRunway

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT QueuesRespectTheirDepth

PROPERTY EveryQueuedFlightLaunches
nl:
An airport's runway allocator holds a departure queue for each runway. A queue has a fixed depth and applies backpressure: while a queue is at depth, ground control will not add another flight to it and the flight waits at the gate instead. Flights leave a queue from the front, in the order they joined. One runway at a time may be closed -- a crosswind, a bird strike, an inspection -- and a closed runway launches nothing until it reopens. The tower supervisor holds a bounded number of privileged cancellations for flights that must come out of a queue without launching.

A flight at the gate may join the back of any runway's queue, provided that queue is below its depth. The flight at the front of an open runway's queue may launch: it leaves the queue and is airborne. A flight that is airborne may return to the gate later in the day. The supervisor may pull any flight out of the middle of any queue, spending one privileged cancellation; the flight goes back to the gate and the flights behind it close up. Ground control may close the one runway that is not already closed, and may reopen the closed runway.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No runway's departure queue is ever longer than that runway's queue depth.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every flight that has joined a departure queue eventually gets airborne.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m5p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Branches, Servers, Copies, NoBranch, NoCopy

\* surfaced[s] is which of server s's grants have actually reached the
\* branches; grants surface in any order, so a branch counts only those.
VARIABLES grant, surfaced, lockedBy, inHand

vars == << grant, surfaced, lockedBy, inHand >>

Surfaced(cp, b) == {s \in Servers : cp \in surfaced[s] /\ grant[s][cp] = b}

TypeOK ==
    /\ grant \in [Servers -> [Copies -> Branches \cup {NoBranch}]]
    /\ surfaced \in [Servers -> SUBSET Copies]
    /\ lockedBy \in [Copies -> Branches \cup {NoBranch}]
    /\ inHand \in [Branches -> Copies \cup {NoCopy}]

Init ==
    /\ grant = [s \in Servers |-> [cp \in Copies |-> NoBranch]]
    /\ surfaced = [s \in Servers |-> {}]
    /\ lockedBy = [cp \in Copies |-> NoBranch]
    /\ inHand = [b \in Branches |-> NoCopy]

\* A server grants a copy once and stands by it until the copy is released.
Grant(s, cp, b) ==
    /\ grant[s][cp] = NoBranch
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![s][cp] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << surfaced, lockedBy, inHand >>

Surface(s, cp) ==
    /\ grant[s][cp] # NoBranch
    /\ cp \notin surfaced[s]
    /\ surfaced' = [surfaced EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {cp}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, lockedBy, inHand >>

TakeRegister(b, cp) ==
    /\ lockedBy[cp] = NoBranch
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Surfaced(cp, b)) > Cardinality(Servers)
    /\ lockedBy' = [lockedBy EXCEPT ![cp] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, surfaced, inHand >>

TakeInHand(b, cp) ==
    /\ lockedBy[cp] = b
    /\ inHand[b] = NoCopy
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![b] = cp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, surfaced, lockedBy >>

PutDown(b) ==
    /\ inHand[b] # NoCopy
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![b] = NoCopy]
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, surfaced, lockedBy >>

\* The register is only handed back once the branch has actually put the copy
\* down; releasing it first is exactly what the safety property forbids.
ReleaseRegister(b, cp) ==
    /\ lockedBy[cp] = b
    /\ inHand[b] # cp
    /\ lockedBy' = [lockedBy EXCEPT ![cp] = NoBranch]
    /\ grant' = [s \in Servers |-> [grant[s] EXCEPT ![cp] = NoBranch]]
    /\ surfaced' = [s \in Servers |-> surfaced[s] \ {cp}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << inHand >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers, cp \in Copies, b \in Branches : Grant(s, cp, b)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, cp \in Copies : Surface(s, cp)
    \/ \E b \in Branches, cp \in Copies : TakeRegister(b, cp) \/ TakeInHand(b, cp) \/ ReleaseRegister(b, cp)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : PutDown(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CopyInHandIsRegistered ==
    \A b \in Branches : inHand[b] # NoCopy => lockedBy[inHand[b]] = b

====
nl:
A library consortium reserves shared copies through its catalogue servers. Only one branch at a time may work a copy's reservation record, and which branch that is is settled by a vote: a branch may take the copy's lock register once a strict majority of the catalogue servers have granted the copy to it. A server grants a copy once and does not change its mind until the copy is released. The grants reach the branches over the consortium's message fabric, which promises nothing about order, so a branch acts on the grants that have actually surfaced to it, in whatever order they surface.

A catalogue server that has not yet granted a copy may grant it to any branch. A grant a server has given may surface to the branches, in any order. A branch may take a copy's lock register when the register is free and the grants that have surfaced give that branch a strict majority of the servers. A branch that holds a copy's lock register may begin working the reservation record, which is the branch recording for itself that the copy is in its hands. A branch working a record may stop working it. A branch that holds a copy's lock register and is no longer working the record may release the register: the register goes free, every server's grant for that copy is cleared, and the grants that had surfaced for it are forgotten, so the next round starts clean.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a branch has the copy in its hands, that copy's lock register names that branch, so two branches never have the same copy in hand at once.

---- MODULE W4Od11m8p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Installs, Presses, Hours, Jobs, NoInstall, NoJob

\* A press hour is addressed coarse-then-fine: the press first, then the hour.
PressHours == Presses \X Hours
PressOf(ph) == ph[1]

VARIABLES pressHeld, register, book, state

vars == << pressHeld, register, book, state >>

Clear(f, j) == [ph \in PressHours |-> IF f[ph] = j THEN NoJob ELSE f[ph]]

TypeOK ==
    /\ pressHeld \in [Presses -> Installs \cup {NoInstall}]
    /\ register \in [PressHours -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]
    /\ book \in [Installs -> [PressHours -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]]
    /\ state \in [Jobs -> {"queued", "booked", "done", "dropped"}]

Init ==
    /\ pressHeld = [p \in Presses |-> NoInstall]
    /\ register = [ph \in PressHours |-> NoJob]
    /\ book = [i \in Installs |-> [ph \in PressHours |-> NoJob]]
    /\ state = [j \in Jobs |-> "queued"]

TakePress(i, p) ==
    /\ pressHeld[p] = NoInstall
    /\ pressHeld' = [pressHeld EXCEPT ![p] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED << register, book, state >>

\* The coarse hold is what stops the other installation writing the same press
\* while this one is deciding which hour to use.
Book(i, j, ph) ==
    /\ pressHeld[PressOf(ph)] = i
    /\ state[j] = "queued"
    /\ register[ph] = NoJob
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![ph] = j]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![i][ph] = j]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "booked"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pressHeld >>

GivePressBack(i, p) ==
    /\ pressHeld[p] = i
    /\ pressHeld' = [pressHeld EXCEPT ![p] = NoInstall]
    /\ UNCHANGED << register, book, state >>

\* Completion clears the job from the register and from every book at once.
Complete(j) ==
    /\ state[j] = "booked"
    /\ register' = Clear(register, j)
    /\ book' = [i \in Installs |-> Clear(book[i], j)]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pressHeld >>

Drop(j) ==
    /\ state[j] = "queued"
    /\ \A ph \in PressHours : register[ph] # NoJob
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "dropped"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pressHeld, register, book >>

Requeue(j) ==
    /\ state[j] \in {"done", "dropped"}
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pressHeld, register, book >>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Installs, p \in Presses : TakePress(i, p) \/ GivePressBack(i, p)
    \/ \E i \in Installs, j \in Jobs, ph \in PressHours : Book(i, j, ph)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Complete(j) \/ Drop(j) \/ Requeue(j)

\* Booking is only enabled while some installation happens to hold the right
\* press, so each job needs strong fairness on its own booking.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A j \in Jobs :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E i \in Installs, ph \in PressHours : Book(i, j, ph))
        /\ SF_vars(Drop(j))
    /\ \A p \in Presses :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(\E i \in Installs : TakePress(i, p))

BooksAgreeWithTheRegister ==
    \A i \in Installs, ph \in PressHours :
        book[i][ph] # NoJob => register[ph] = book[i][ph]

EveryQueuedJobSettles ==
    \A j \in Jobs : (state[j] = "queued") ~> (state[j] \in {"booked", "dropped"})

====
nl:
A print shop ended up with two spooler installations, each sold as the shop's only one, and both now book work onto the same pool of presses. A booking is a press hour: a particular press for a particular hour of the shift. The pool keeps one authoritative register of who has each press hour; each installation also keeps its own book, which is what its operators actually look at. Booking is done coarse then fine: an installation must hold the press before it may write any of that press's hours, so the two installations cannot be writing the same press at the same moment.

An installation may take a press that no installation is holding. An installation holding a press may book a queued job onto one of that press's hours, provided the pool register shows that hour free: the register records the job, the installation's own book records the job, and the job counts as booked. An installation may give a press back; the bookings it already made stay in place. A booked job may run to completion, which clears that job from the pool register and from every installation's book. A queued job may be dropped when no press hour is free in the register. A job that has completed or been dropped may be queued again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Wherever an installation's own book has a job against a press hour, the pool's authoritative register has the same job against that same press hour, so the two installations never hold different jobs for one press hour.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every queued job is eventually either booked onto a press hour or dropped.

---- MODULE W4Od4m9p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, TotalLitres, MaxEpoch

\* Every litre is in a tank, in the line, or in the sump. Each action below
\* moves one litre out of exactly one place and into exactly one other.
VARIABLES tank, line, sump, epoch, stationEpoch, dead

vars == << tank, line, sump, epoch, stationEpoch, dead >>

RECURSIVE Tally(_)
Tally(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET st == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN tank[st] + Tally(S \ {st})

TypeOK ==
    /\ tank \in [Stations -> 0..TotalLitres]
    /\ line \in 0..TotalLitres
    /\ sump \in 0..TotalLitres
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ stationEpoch \in [Stations -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ dead \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ tank = [st \in Stations |-> IF st = CHOOSE x \in Stations : TRUE THEN TotalLitres ELSE 0]
    /\ line = 0
    /\ sump = 0
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ stationEpoch = [st \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ dead = FALSE

Draw(st) ==
    /\ stationEpoch[st] = epoch
    /\ tank[st] > 0
    /\ tank' = [tank EXCEPT ![st] = @ - 1]
    /\ line' = line + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << sump, epoch, stationEpoch, dead >>

Dispense ==
    /\ line > 0
    /\ line' = line - 1
    /\ sump' = sump + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << tank, epoch, stationEpoch, dead >>

ReturnToTank(st) ==
    /\ line > 0
    /\ line' = line - 1
    /\ tank' = [tank EXCEPT ![st] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << sump, epoch, stationEpoch, dead >>

Reclaim(st) ==
    /\ sump > 0
    /\ sump' = sump - 1
    /\ tank' = [tank EXCEPT ![st] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << line, epoch, stationEpoch, dead >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ ~dead
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << tank, line, sump, stationEpoch, dead >>

Resync(st) ==
    /\ stationEpoch[st] # epoch
    /\ stationEpoch' = [stationEpoch EXCEPT ![st] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << tank, line, sump, epoch, dead >>

\* A silent crash: the recipe schedule simply stops moving.
Crash ==
    /\ ~dead
    /\ dead' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED << tank, line, sump, epoch, stationEpoch >>

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Stations : Draw(st) \/ ReturnToTank(st) \/ Reclaim(st) \/ Resync(st)
    \/ Dispense \/ Reconfigure \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DetergentIsConserved == Tally(Stations) + line + sump = TotalLitres

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Stations = {stnA, stnB}
    TotalLitres = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DetergentIsConserved
nl:
A car-wash conveyor doses detergent from a set of station tanks. Every litre the site holds is in exactly one of three places: sitting in a station tank, in the dosing line on its way to a car, or already used on cars and collected in the reclaim sump. Nothing is added and nothing evaporates; the site's total is what it is. The dosing controller is reconfigured whenever the chemical recipe changes, which advances its dosing epoch, and a station will only draw once it has resynchronised to the controller's current epoch. The controller can crash silently: it simply stops changing recipes, with no announcement, and the epoch it last broadcast stays latched at the stations.

A station that has resynchronised to the current epoch and has detergent in its tank may draw one litre into the dosing line. A litre in the dosing line may be dispensed onto a car, which puts it in the reclaim sump. A litre in the dosing line may instead be returned to any station's tank. A litre in the reclaim sump may be reclaimed back into any station's tank by the site's recovery plant. The controller may reconfigure while it is alive and has recipes left in its schedule, advancing the epoch. A station whose latched epoch is behind the controller's may resynchronise. The controller may crash, after which it never reconfigures again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The detergent in all the station tanks plus the detergent in the dosing line plus the detergent in the reclaim sump always sums to the site's total, so dosing never creates or loses a litre.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Depots, Allocation, NoDepot, NoRead

\* readOn/readVal are the drone's outstanding reading of a depot counter; the
\* write only lands if the counter still agrees with it.
VARIABLES remaining, issued, carrying, readOn, readVal

vars == << remaining, issued, carrying, readOn, readVal >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ remaining \in [Depots -> 0..Allocation]
    /\ issued \in [Depots -> 0..Allocation]
    /\ carrying \in [Drones -> Depots \cup {NoDepot}]
    /\ readOn \in [Drones -> Depots \cup {NoDepot}]
    /\ readVal \in [Drones -> (0..Allocation) \cup {NoRead}]

Init ==
    /\ remaining = [dp \in Depots |-> Allocation]
    /\ issued = [dp \in Depots |-> 0]
    /\ carrying = [d \in Drones |-> NoDepot]
    /\ readOn = [d \in Drones |-> NoDepot]
    /\ readVal = [d \in Drones |-> NoRead]

ReadLevel(d, dp) ==
    /\ carrying[d] = NoDepot
    /\ readOn[d] = NoDepot
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![d] = dp]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = remaining[dp]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << remaining, issued, carrying >>

\* The unit leaves the depot and joins the issued total in the same step, so
\* the depot's books cannot come apart even when a read went stale.
TakeLoad(d) ==
    /\ readOn[d] # NoDepot
    /\ readVal[d] = remaining[readOn[d]]
    /\ readVal[d] > 0
    /\ remaining' = [remaining EXCEPT ![readOn[d]] = readVal[d] - 1]
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![readOn[d]] = @ + 1]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![d] = readOn[d]]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoDepot]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = NoRead]

DiscardRead(d) ==
    /\ readOn[d] # NoDepot
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoDepot]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << remaining, issued, carrying >>

DropLoad(d) ==
    /\ carrying[d] # NoDepot
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![d] = NoDepot]
    /\ UNCHANGED << remaining, issued, readOn, readVal >>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones, dp \in Depots : ReadLevel(d, dp)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : TakeLoad(d) \/ DiscardRead(d) \/ DropLoad(d)

\* Nothing can block a drop, so weak fairness per drone is enough.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A d \in Drones :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(DropLoad(d))

DepotBooksBalance ==
    \A dp \in Depots : remaining[dp] + issued[dp] = Allocation

EveryLoadIsDropped ==
    \A d \in Drones : (carrying[d] # NoDepot) ~> (carrying[d] = NoDepot)

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {drA, drB}
    Depots = {dpNorth, dpSouth}
    Allocation = 2
    NoDepot = noDepot
    NoRead = noRead

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DepotBooksBalance

PROPERTY EveryLoadIsDropped
nl:
A wildfire air operation loads retardant from several depots. Each depot was allocated a fixed quantity for the incident, and every unit of that allocation is either still in the depot or has been issued to a drone -- the operation's ledger has to account for the whole allocation at all times. Depot levels are held in a single counter per depot, and drones take a load by compare-and-swap: a drone reads a depot's counter, then writes back its read minus one only if the counter still holds what it read. Level telemetry reaches the drones over the incident radio, which makes no ordering promise, so what a drone read may already be out of date by the time it writes.

A drone carrying nothing and holding no reading may read any depot's counter, remembering the depot and the number it saw. A drone whose reading still matches that depot's counter, and whose reading was above zero, may take a load: the counter becomes its reading minus one, the depot's issued total goes up by one, and the drone is carrying that depot's retardant. A drone may discard a reading it is holding. A drone carrying a load may drop it on the fire, after which it carries nothing; the load stays on the depot's issued total, because it did leave the depot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every depot, the units still in the depot plus the units it has issued always equal that depot's allocation for the incident.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every drone that is carrying a load eventually drops it.

---- MODULE W4Od3m2p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, Instructions, Amount, MaxWindow

\* Every unit of an instruction sits in exactly one of owed, inflight, settled;
\* each action below moves units between them and never changes the total.
VARIABLES owed, inflight, settled, pledged, window

vars == << owed, inflight, settled, pledged, window >>

RECURSIVE Tally(_)
Tally(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET i == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN inflight[i] + Tally(S \ {i})

InFlightTotal == Tally(Instructions)

TypeOK ==
    /\ owed \in [Instructions -> 0..Amount]
    /\ inflight \in [Instructions -> 0..Amount]
    /\ settled \in [Instructions -> 0..Amount]
    /\ pledged \in [Instructions -> SUBSET Members]
    /\ window \in 0..MaxWindow

Init ==
    /\ owed = [i \in Instructions |-> Amount]
    /\ inflight = [i \in Instructions |-> 0]
    /\ settled = [i \in Instructions |-> 0]
    /\ pledged = [i \in Instructions |-> {}]
    /\ window = 1

Pledge(m, i) ==
    /\ m \notin pledged[i]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {m}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owed, inflight, settled, window >>

\* Unanimity of the member banks is what lets a unit leave owed at all.
Launch(i) ==
    /\ \A m \in Members : m \in pledged[i]
    /\ owed[i] > 0
    /\ InFlightTotal < window
    /\ owed' = [owed EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ inflight' = [inflight EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << settled, pledged, window >>

SettleOne(i) ==
    /\ inflight[i] > 0
    /\ inflight' = [inflight EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ settled' = [settled EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owed, pledged, window >>

\* An abort puts every in-flight unit of the instruction back where it came
\* from, in one movement, and gives the pledges back.
Abort(i) ==
    /\ inflight[i] > 0
    /\ owed' = [owed EXCEPT ![i] = @ + inflight[i]]
    /\ inflight' = [inflight EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << settled, window >>

Reprovision(w) ==
    /\ w # window
    /\ w >= InFlightTotal
    /\ window' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED << owed, inflight, settled, pledged >>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members, i \in Instructions : Pledge(m, i)
    \/ \E i \in Instructions : Launch(i) \/ SettleOne(i) \/ Abort(i)
    \/ \E w \in 0..MaxWindow : Reprovision(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EveryInstructionAccountsForItsAmount ==
    \A i \in Instructions : owed[i] + inflight[i] + settled[i] = Amount

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Members = {mbrA, mbrB}
    Instructions = {ixn1, ixn2}
    Amount = 2
    MaxWindow = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT EveryInstructionAccountsForItsAmount
nl:
A clearing house settles a fixed set of interbank instructions. Each instruction is for a fixed amount, and every unit of that amount is at all times in exactly one of three states: still owed, in flight through the settlement machinery, or finally settled. The clearing house moves units between those states and never invents or destroys one. Moving units into flight is agreed by a two-phase commit across the member banks, and the settlement window limits how many units may be in flight across all instructions at once. That window is re-provisioned during the day as liquidity comes and goes, though never below what is already in flight.

A member bank may pledge to an instruction it has not yet pledged to. An instruction that every member bank has pledged to, and that still has units owed, may move one unit into flight, provided the units already in flight across all instructions are below the settlement window. An instruction with units in flight may settle one of them, moving it to settled. An instruction with units in flight may instead be aborted, which returns every one of its in-flight units to owed and releases all of its pledges. The clearing house may re-provision the settlement window to any different value that is not below the units currently in flight.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every instruction, the units still owed plus the units in flight plus the units settled always equal that instruction's amount.

---- MODULE W4Od2m5p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Containers, NoVote

\* Each container is staged with exactly one seal authority; sealing spends it,
\* and the pair below is what makes the seal once-only.
VARIABLES authority, seals, voted, surfaced, busUp

vars == << authority, seals, voted, surfaced, busUp >>

Carried(c) == {k \in Controllers : c \in surfaced[k] /\ c \in voted[k]}
Majority(c) == 2 * Cardinality(Carried(c)) > Cardinality(Controllers)

TypeOK ==
    /\ authority \in [Containers -> 0..1]
    /\ seals \in [Containers -> 0..1]
    /\ voted \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Containers]
    /\ surfaced \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Containers]
    /\ busUp \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ authority = [c \in Containers |-> 1]
    /\ seals = [c \in Containers |-> 0]
    /\ voted = [k \in Controllers |-> {}]
    /\ surfaced = [k \in Controllers |-> {}]
    /\ busUp = TRUE

CastVote(k, c) ==
    /\ busUp
    /\ c \notin voted[k]
    /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![k] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << authority, seals, surfaced, busUp >>

\* Votes surface at the station in any order at all.
SurfaceVote(k, c) ==
    /\ c \in voted[k]
    /\ c \notin surfaced[k]
    /\ surfaced' = [surfaced EXCEPT ![k] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << authority, seals, voted, busUp >>

Seal(c) ==
    /\ Majority(c)
    /\ authority[c] = 1
    /\ authority' = [authority EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
    /\ seals' = [seals EXCEPT ![c] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << voted, surfaced, busUp >>

BusDown == /\ busUp /\ busUp' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED << authority, seals, voted, surfaced >>
BusRestored == /\ ~busUp /\ busUp' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED << authority, seals, voted, surfaced >>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Controllers, c \in Containers : CastVote(k, c) \/ SurfaceVote(k, c)
    \/ \E c \in Containers : Seal(c)
    \/ BusDown \/ BusRestored

\* Voting is blocked while the charging bus is down, so casting needs strong
\* fairness; votes are never withdrawn, so once a majority has surfaced it
\* stays and weak fairness is enough for the seal itself.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A k \in Controllers :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ \A c \in Containers :
            /\ TRUE
            /\ SF_vars(CastVote(k, c))
            /\ WF_vars(SurfaceVote(k, c))
    /\ \A c \in Containers :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Seal(c))
    /\ WF_vars(BusRestored)

SealAuthorityIsSpentExactlyOnce ==
    \A c \in Containers : authority[c] + seals[c] = 1

EveryContainerIsEventuallySealed ==
    \A c \in Containers : (seals[c] = 0) ~> (seals[c] = 1)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctl1, ctl2, ctl3}
    Containers = {cnt1, cnt2}
    NoVote = noVote

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SealAuthorityIsSpentExactlyOnce

PROPERTY EveryContainerIsEventuallySealed
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet seals outbound containers. Sealing is irreversible: once a container is sealed the manifest is committed to the carrier and the fleet has no way to open it again, so a container must never be sealed twice. Each container is issued exactly one seal authority when it is staged, and sealing spends it. Whether a container is ready to seal is decided by a vote of the fleet controllers: a container may be sealed once a strict majority of the controllers have voted for it and those votes have actually reached the sealing station. Votes travel over the warehouse radio, which promises nothing about order, so the votes surface at the station in whatever order they arrive. The fleet also runs off a charging bus that is periodically taken down; controllers do not vote while it is down.

A controller may vote for a container it has not yet voted for, provided the charging bus is up. A vote a controller has cast may surface at the sealing station, in any order. A container whose surfaced votes give it a strict majority of the controllers, and whose seal authority is unspent, may be sealed: the authority is spent and the seal is recorded. The charging bus may be taken down, and a bus that is down may be brought back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every container, its unspent seal authorities plus its recorded seals always sum to exactly one, so no container is ever sealed twice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every staged container is eventually sealed.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS BerthSide, GateSide, Carriers, Berths, BerthLimit, MaxTerm, NoCtl, NoBerth

\* Two separately installed control systems, one pool of carriers between them.
Controllers == BerthSide \cup GateSide

\* A carrier that has been dispatched but has not arrived yet already occupies
\* its berth's working room, so both terms are counted against the limit.
VARIABLES term, backing, chair, atBerth, enRoute

vars == << term, backing, chair, atBerth, enRoute >>

Working(b) ==
    Cardinality({c \in Carriers : atBerth[c] = b})
      + Cardinality({c \in Carriers : enRoute[c] = b})
Backers(n) == {k \in Controllers : backing[k] = n}

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ backing \in [Controllers -> Controllers \cup {NoCtl}]
    /\ chair \in Controllers \cup {NoCtl}
    /\ atBerth \in [Carriers -> Berths \cup {NoBerth}]
    /\ enRoute \in [Carriers -> Berths \cup {NoBerth}]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ backing = [k \in Controllers |-> NoCtl]
    /\ chair = NoCtl
    /\ atBerth = [c \in Carriers |-> NoBerth]
    /\ enRoute = [c \in Carriers |-> NoBerth]

\* A controller may move its backing at any time; what it cannot do is unseat
\* a dispatcher that is already in the chair.
Back(k, n) ==
    /\ backing[k] # n
    /\ backing' = [backing EXCEPT ![k] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, chair, atBerth, enRoute >>

\* The chair is only taken on a strict majority of the controllers, which is
\* what stops the two installations dispatching at once.
TakeChair(n) ==
    /\ chair = NoCtl
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(n)) > Cardinality(Controllers)
    /\ chair' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, atBerth, enRoute >>

Dispatch(c, b) ==
    /\ chair # NoCtl
    /\ atBerth[c] = NoBerth
    /\ enRoute[c] = NoBerth
    /\ Working(b) < BerthLimit
    /\ enRoute' = [enRoute EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, atBerth >>

Arrive(c) ==
    /\ enRoute[c] # NoBerth
    /\ atBerth' = [atBerth EXCEPT ![c] = enRoute[c]]
    /\ enRoute' = [enRoute EXCEPT ![c] = NoBerth]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair >>

Recall(c) ==
    /\ chair # NoCtl
    /\ atBerth[c] # NoBerth
    /\ atBerth' = [atBerth EXCEPT ![c] = NoBerth]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, enRoute >>

\* A failover empties the chair and voids every backing; the carriers already
\* at berths are not moved by it.
FailOver ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ chair' = NoCtl
    /\ backing' = [k \in Controllers |-> NoCtl]
    /\ UNCHANGED << atBerth, enRoute >>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Controllers, n \in Controllers : Back(k, n)
    \/ \E n \in Controllers : TakeChair(n)
    \/ \E c \in Carriers, b \in Berths : Dispatch(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Carriers : Arrive(c) \/ Recall(c)
    \/ FailOver

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoBerthIsOverworked == \A b \in Berths : Working(b) <= BerthLimit

====
nl:
A container terminal ended up with two yard control systems, the old berth-side one and the new gate-side one, each installed as if it were the only one. Both dispatch the same pool of straddle carriers. Which controller may dispatch is settled by election: a controller becomes the dispatcher for a term once a strict majority of the controllers have backed it in that term. Only the sitting dispatcher moves carriers. Each berth can work only so many carriers at once, and that limit is what the terminal's civil engineering allows.

A controller may back any controller it is not already backing. A controller backed by a strict majority in the current term may take the dispatcher's chair, if the chair is empty. The sitting dispatcher may dispatch a carrier that is standing down and not already under way to a berth, provided that berth is working fewer carriers than its limit -- a carrier under way to a berth counts against that berth exactly as one already there does, because the room has to be kept for it. A carrier under way may arrive, taking its place at the berth. The sitting dispatcher may recall a carrier from a berth, standing it down. The terminal may fail the chair over while it has terms left in its schedule: the term advances, the chair is emptied, and every controller's backing is cleared, so the next dispatcher must be elected afresh. Carriers already at berths stay where they are across a failover.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No berth is ever working more straddle carriers, counting those already there and those under way to it, than that berth's limit.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Matches, MaxTerm, MaxLimit, NoNode, NoMatch

\* chairTerm is the term the chair was taken in; a chair left over from an
\* earlier term is not a licence to assemble.
VARIABLES term, backing, chair, chairTerm, building, limit

vars == << term, backing, chair, chairTerm, building, limit >>

Assembling == Cardinality({n \in Nodes : building[n] # NoMatch})
Backers(n) == {k \in Nodes : backing[k] = n}

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ backing \in [Nodes -> Nodes \cup {NoNode}]
    /\ chair \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}
    /\ chairTerm \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ building \in [Nodes -> Matches \cup {NoMatch}]
    /\ limit \in 0..MaxLimit

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ backing = [k \in Nodes |-> NoNode]
    /\ chair = NoNode
    /\ chairTerm = 0
    /\ building = [n \in Nodes |-> NoMatch]
    /\ limit = 1

Back(k, n) ==
    /\ backing[k] # n
    /\ backing' = [backing EXCEPT ![k] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, chair, chairTerm, building, limit >>

TakeChair(n) ==
    /\ chair = NoNode
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(n)) > Cardinality(Nodes)
    /\ chair' = n
    /\ chairTerm' = term
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, building, limit >>

BeginAssembly(n, m) ==
    /\ chair = n
    /\ chairTerm = term
    /\ building[n] = NoMatch
    /\ Assembling < limit
    /\ building' = [building EXCEPT ![n] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, chairTerm, limit >>

Release(n) ==
    /\ building[n] # NoMatch
    /\ building' = [building EXCEPT ![n] = NoMatch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, chairTerm, limit >>

\* A failover tears down whatever was being assembled, because the node in the
\* chair may be exactly the one that stopped answering.
FailOver ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ chair' = NoNode
    /\ backing' = [k \in Nodes |-> NoNode]
    /\ building' = [n \in Nodes |-> NoMatch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << chairTerm, limit >>

SetLimit(l) ==
    /\ l # limit
    /\ l >= Assembling
    /\ limit' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, chairTerm, building >>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Nodes, n \in Nodes : Back(k, n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : TakeChair(n) \/ Release(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, m \in Matches : BeginAssembly(n, m)
    \/ \E l \in 0..MaxLimit : SetLimit(l)
    \/ FailOver

\* Nothing blocks a release, so weak fairness per node is enough.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A n \in Nodes :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Release(n))

OnlyTheCurrentChairAssembles ==
    \A n \in Nodes :
        building[n] # NoMatch => (chair = n /\ chairTerm = term)

EveryAssemblyIsReleased ==
    \A n \in Nodes : (building[n] # NoMatch) ~> (building[n] = NoMatch)

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {lobA, lobB, lobC}
    Matches = {mtch1}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxLimit = 2
    NoNode = noNode
    NoMatch = noMatch

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlyTheCurrentChairAssembles

PROPERTY EveryAssemblyIsReleased
nl:
A multiplayer game runs its lobby matchmaking across a set of nodes, but only one node at a time may be assembling matches: assembling is the critical section, because two nodes assembling at once would hand the same players to two different servers. Which node it is is settled by election with failover -- a node takes the coordinator's chair once a strict majority of the nodes back it, and the chair is stamped with the term it was taken in. The operators fail the chair over when a node stops answering, which advances the term, empties the chair, clears every backing, and tears down whatever was being assembled, since the node that was assembling may be the one that went away. How many matches may be under assembly at once is a runtime setting the operators raise and lower with demand, never below what is already being assembled.

A node may back any node it is not already backing. A node backed by a strict majority may take the coordinator's chair when the chair is empty, stamping it with the current term. The node in the chair, if its chair stamp is still the current term, may begin assembling a match, provided the matches under assembly are below the current setting. A node that is assembling may finish, releasing the match. The operators may fail the chair over while they have failovers left in their schedule. The operators may set the assembly limit to any different value that is not below the number of matches under assembly.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A node is only ever assembling a match while it is the node in the coordinator's chair and that chair was stamped in the current term.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every match that is under assembly is eventually released.

---- MODULE W4Od1m0p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Runways, MaxVersion, NoStamp, NoCtl

\* snap[c] is c's open write attempt against the plan; taking a clearance
\* closes it, and decertifying discards it.
VARIABLES version, snap, cleared, certified, offHeadset

vars == << version, snap, cleared, certified, offHeadset >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ cleared \in [Runways -> Controllers \cup {NoCtl}]
    /\ certified \in SUBSET Controllers
    /\ offHeadset \in Controllers \cup {NoCtl}

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> NoStamp]
    /\ cleared = [r \in Runways |-> NoCtl]
    /\ certified = {}
    /\ offHeadset = NoCtl

ReadPlan(c) ==
    /\ c # offHeadset
    /\ snap[c] = NoStamp
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, cleared, certified, offHeadset >>

\* The version test and the certification test are both taken at the moment
\* the clearance lands, and the attempt is closed in the same step.
TakeClearance(c, r) ==
    /\ c # offHeadset
    /\ snap[c] = version
    /\ c \in certified
    /\ cleared[r] = NoCtl
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << certified, offHeadset >>

Retry(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoStamp
    /\ snap[c] # version
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, cleared, certified, offHeadset >>

GiveUp(c, r) ==
    /\ cleared[r] = c
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![r] = NoCtl]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, certified, offHeadset >>

Certify(c) ==
    /\ c \notin certified
    /\ certified' = certified \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, cleared, offHeadset >>

\* Decertification reaches the controller in the same movement, so it can only
\* be applied to one the supervisor can actually reach.
Decertify(c) ==
    /\ c \in certified
    /\ c # offHeadset
    /\ certified' = certified \ {c}
    /\ cleared' = [r \in Runways |-> IF cleared[r] = c THEN NoCtl ELSE cleared[r]]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, offHeadset >>

GoOff(c) == /\ offHeadset = NoCtl /\ offHeadset' = c /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, cleared, certified >>
ComeBack == /\ offHeadset # NoCtl /\ offHeadset' = NoCtl /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, cleared, certified >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ReadPlan(c) \/ Retry(c) \/ Certify(c) \/ Decertify(c) \/ GoOff(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : TakeClearance(c, r) \/ GiveUp(c, r)
    \/ ComeBack

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A clearance outlives the write attempt that produced it, but never outlives
\* its holder's certification.
EveryClearanceIsHeldByACertifiedController ==
    \A r \in Runways : cleared[r] # NoCtl => cleared[r] \in certified

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {appA, appB}
    Runways = {rwy09, rwy27}
    MaxVersion = 3
    NoStamp = noStamp
    NoCtl = noCtl

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT EveryClearanceIsHeldByACertifiedController
nl:
An airport's runway allocator holds one clearance plan that all approach controllers write to. Nobody locks the plan: a controller reads it, taking its version stamp, and its write only lands if the stamp is unchanged; otherwise it retries. Writing a clearance is a certified act -- only a controller currently on the certification list may hold a runway clearance, and the watch supervisor adds and removes controllers from that list as shifts and ratings change. Controllers are slow rather than failed: at most one controller at a time is off headset, and they always come back, but the supervisor will not decertify a controller it cannot reach.

A controller on headset holding no snapshot may read the plan, taking its version stamp. A controller on headset whose snapshot stamp still matches the plan, who is on the certification list, may take a clearance on a runway that nobody holds: the clearance is recorded against it, the plan's version stamp advances, and its snapshot is closed in the same movement. A controller whose snapshot stamp no longer matches the plan retries, discarding it. A controller may give up a clearance it holds. The supervisor may add a controller to the certification list. The supervisor may decertify a controller it can reach, which strikes that controller off the list, drops every clearance it holds, and discards its snapshot. Finally, the one controller on headset may go off headset, and the controller off headset may come back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every runway clearance is held by a controller that is on the certification list.

---- MODULE W4Od13m8p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Vans, Routes, Stops, TrafficLimit, MaxReleases, NoRoute, NoMachine

\* A machine is addressed coarse-then-fine: the route first, then the stop.
Machines == Routes \X Stops
RouteOf(m) == m[1]

\* An assigned van already occupies road space on its route, so both terms
\* below count against the limit.
VARIABLES holdsRoute, job, working, releases

vars == << holdsRoute, job, working, releases >>

Traffic(rt) ==
    Cardinality({v \in Vans : job[v] # NoMachine /\ RouteOf(job[v]) = rt /\ ~working[v]})
      + Cardinality({v \in Vans : job[v] # NoMachine /\ RouteOf(job[v]) = rt /\ working[v]})

TypeOK ==
    /\ holdsRoute \in [Vans -> Routes \cup {NoRoute}]
    /\ job \in [Vans -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]
    /\ working \in [Vans -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ releases \in 0..MaxReleases

Init ==
    /\ holdsRoute = [v \in Vans |-> NoRoute]
    /\ job = [v \in Vans |-> NoMachine]
    /\ working = [v \in Vans |-> FALSE]
    /\ releases = 0

TakeRoute(v, rt) ==
    /\ holdsRoute[v] = NoRoute
    /\ \A w \in Vans : holdsRoute[w] # rt
    /\ holdsRoute' = [holdsRoute EXCEPT ![v] = rt]
    /\ UNCHANGED << job, working, releases >>

Assign(v, m) ==
    /\ holdsRoute[v] = RouteOf(m)
    /\ job[v] = NoMachine
    /\ \A w \in Vans : job[w] # m
    /\ Traffic(RouteOf(m)) < TrafficLimit
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![v] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED << holdsRoute, working, releases >>

Arrive(v) ==
    /\ job[v] # NoMachine
    /\ ~working[v]
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![v] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << holdsRoute, job, releases >>

Finish(v) ==
    /\ working[v]
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![v] = NoMachine]
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![v] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << holdsRoute, releases >>

GiveRouteBack(v) ==
    /\ holdsRoute[v] # NoRoute
    /\ job[v] = NoMachine
    /\ holdsRoute' = [holdsRoute EXCEPT ![v] = NoRoute]
    /\ UNCHANGED << job, working, releases >>

\* The manager's release surrenders the fine and the coarse hold together.
PrivilegedRelease(v) ==
    /\ releases < MaxReleases
    /\ \/ holdsRoute[v] # NoRoute
       \/ job[v] # NoMachine
    /\ holdsRoute' = [holdsRoute EXCEPT ![v] = NoRoute]
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![v] = NoMachine]
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![v] = FALSE]
    /\ releases' = releases + 1

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Vans, rt \in Routes : TakeRoute(v, rt)
    \/ \E v \in Vans, m \in Machines : Assign(v, m)
    \/ \E v \in Vans : Arrive(v) \/ Finish(v) \/ GiveRouteBack(v) \/ PrivilegedRelease(v)

\* Arriving and finishing are never blocked by anything else, so weak fairness
\* per van closes out every assignment.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A v \in Vans :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Arrive(v))
        /\ WF_vars(Finish(v))

RouteTrafficWithinLimit == \A rt \in Routes : Traffic(rt) <= TrafficLimit

EveryAssignmentIsWorkedOff ==
    \A v \in Vans : (job[v] # NoMachine) ~> (job[v] = NoMachine)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Vans = {vanA, vanB}
    Routes = {rteN, rteS}
    Stops = {stp1, stp2}
    TrafficLimit = 1
    MaxReleases = 1
    NoRoute = noRoute
    NoMachine = noMachine

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RouteTrafficWithinLimit

PROPERTY EveryAssignmentIsWorkedOff
nl:
A vending operator services machines from a depot. Machines are grouped into routes, and a service van must take the route before it may take any machine on that route -- coarse first, then fine. Each route can only absorb so much service traffic at once: a van that has been assigned a machine on a route counts against that route's traffic limit from the moment it is assigned, not from the moment it arrives, because the route planner has to keep the road space for it. The depot manager holds a privileged release for vans that have gone silent mid-round.

A van holding nothing may take a route that no van holds. A van holding a route may be assigned a machine on that route that no van is assigned, provided the vans already assigned to that route plus the vans already working machines on it are below the route's traffic limit. A van assigned a machine may arrive at it and start working. A van working a machine may finish, which drops the machine. A van holding a route and assigned no machine on it may give the route back. The depot manager may use a privileged release on any van, spending one release: the van's machine and its route are both given up at once, whatever state it was in.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every route, the vans assigned to machines on it plus the vans working machines on it never exceed that route's traffic limit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every van that has been assigned a machine eventually stops being assigned to it.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Keys, Slots, Free, NoSlot, NoRead

\* readOn/readVal are the key's outstanding read of a slot register; booked is
\* what the guest's phone shows, which must never outrun the register.
VARIABLES reg, readOn, readVal, booked

vars == << reg, readOn, readVal, booked >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Slots -> Keys \cup {Free}]
    /\ readOn \in [Keys -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ readVal \in [Keys -> Keys \cup {Free, NoRead}]
    /\ booked \in [Keys -> SUBSET Slots]

Init ==
    /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ readOn = [k \in Keys |-> NoSlot]
    /\ readVal = [k \in Keys |-> NoRead]
    /\ booked = [k \in Keys |-> {}]

ReadSlot(k, s) ==
    /\ readOn[k] = NoSlot
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![k] = s]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![k] = reg[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, booked >>

\* The compare half: a register that moved under the key invalidates the claim.
Claim(k) ==
    /\ readOn[k] # NoSlot
    /\ readVal[k] = Free
    /\ reg[readOn[k]] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![readOn[k]] = k]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![k] = NoSlot]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![k] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << booked >>

StaleRead(k) ==
    /\ readOn[k] # NoSlot
    /\ readVal[k] # reg[readOn[k]]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![k] = NoSlot]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![k] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, booked >>

ShowBooking(k, s) ==
    /\ reg[s] = k
    /\ s \notin booked[k]
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![k] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, readOn, readVal >>

Release(k, s) ==
    /\ s \in booked[k]
    /\ reg[s] = k
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![k] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED << readOn, readVal >>

\* The homeowner's override reassigns the register and strikes the slot from
\* the booked lists it has just invalidated, in one movement.
Override(s, k) ==
    /\ reg[s] # k
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = k]
    /\ booked' = [j \in Keys |-> IF j = k THEN booked[j] ELSE booked[j] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << readOn, readVal >>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Keys, s \in Slots : ReadSlot(k, s) \/ ShowBooking(k, s) \/ Release(k, s) \/ Override(s, k)
    \/ \E k \in Keys : Claim(k) \/ StaleRead(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BookedSlotsAreRegistered ==
    \A k \in Keys, s \in Slots : s \in booked[k] => reg[s] = k

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Keys = {keyA, keyB}
    Slots = {slotMorning, slotEvening}
    Free = free
    NoSlot = noSlot
    NoRead = noRead

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BookedSlotsAreRegistered
nl:
A smart-home hub hands out guest access windows: fixed slots during which a guest key may open the front door. A slot belongs to at most one key. Each slot has a register in the hub that either reads free or names the key that owns it, and keys claim slots by compare-and-swap: a key reads a slot's register, then writes its own name in only if the register still reads what it read. A key also keeps its own list of the slots it believes it booked, which is what the guest's phone shows them. The homeowner holds an override that reassigns a slot outright.

A key holding no outstanding read may read any slot's register, remembering the slot and what it saw. A key whose read still matches that slot's register, and whose read said the slot was free, may claim it: the register takes the key's name and the read is cleared. A key whose remembered value no longer matches discards the read. A key named by a slot's register may write that slot into its own booked list. A key may release a slot it has booked: the slot leaves its booked list and the register goes free in the same movement. The homeowner may override a slot to any key: the register takes that key's name, and the slot is struck from every other key's booked list at the same time, because those bookings are no longer good.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot in a key's booked list is registered to that key, so no slot is ever booked by two different keys.

---- MODULE W4Od9m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Commands, QueueDepth

\* accepted is what the console told the operator it had taken; the safety
\* property is that nothing accepted can fall between the queue and the schedule.
VARIABLES queue, accepted, schedule, busQuiet

vars == << queue, accepted, schedule, busQuiet >>

Waiting(c) == \E i \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i] = c

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Commands)
    /\ Len(queue) <= QueueDepth
    /\ accepted \in SUBSET Commands
    /\ schedule \in SUBSET Commands
    /\ busQuiet \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ accepted = {}
    /\ schedule = {}
    /\ busQuiet = FALSE

\* Backpressure: the console refuses rather than the queue overflowing.
Accept(c) ==
    /\ c \notin accepted
    /\ Len(queue) < QueueDepth
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, c)
    /\ accepted' = accepted \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << schedule, busQuiet >>

\* The command leaves the queue and joins the schedule in the same step, which
\* is the only reason nothing can fall between them.
Apply(c) ==
    /\ ~busQuiet
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue) = c
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ schedule' = schedule \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << accepted, busQuiet >>

GoQuiet == /\ ~busQuiet /\ busQuiet' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED << queue, accepted, schedule >>
Answer  == /\ busQuiet /\ busQuiet' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED << queue, accepted, schedule >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Commands : Accept(c) \/ Apply(c)
    \/ GoQuiet \/ Answer

\* A command's own application is only enabled once it reaches the front of the
\* queue and the bus is answering, so it needs strong fairness.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A c \in Commands :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(Apply(c))
    /\ WF_vars(Answer)

NoAcceptedCommandIsLost ==
    \A c \in Commands : c \in accepted => (Waiting(c) \/ c \in schedule)

EveryAcceptedCommandIsScheduled ==
    \A c \in Commands : (c \in accepted) ~> (c \in schedule)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Commands = {shed1, shed2, shed3}
    QueueDepth = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoAcceptedCommandIsLost

PROPERTY EveryAcceptedCommandIsScheduled
nl:
A grid operator queues load-shedding commands to the relay bus. The queue is bounded and applies backpressure: while it is at depth the operator's console refuses new commands rather than dropping anything already accepted. A command the console has accepted is either still waiting in the queue or has been applied to the shed schedule -- an accepted command that is in neither place would be a shed instruction the operator believes was taken and that never happened. Commands leave the queue from the front, in order. The relay bus is slow rather than failed: it stops accepting applications for a while and then starts again.

The console may accept a command it has not accepted before, provided the queue is below its depth; the command joins the back of the queue and is recorded as accepted. While the relay bus is responsive, the command at the front of the queue may be applied: it leaves the queue and joins the shed schedule. The relay bus may go quiet, and a quiet bus may start answering again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every command the console has accepted is either still waiting in the queue or already in the shed schedule.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every accepted command eventually reaches the shed schedule.

---- MODULE W4Od10m0p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Signallers, Trains, Sections, SectionLimit, MaxVersion, NoSection, NoStamp

\* A cleared-but-not-arrived train holds room in its section, so both terms
\* below count against the limit.
VARIABLES version, snap, berthed, clearedTo, toldOf

vars == << version, snap, berthed, clearedTo, toldOf >>

Occupancy(sec) ==
    Cardinality({t \in Trains : berthed[t] = sec})
      + Cardinality({t \in Trains : clearedTo[t] = sec})

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ snap \in [Signallers -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ berthed \in [Trains -> Sections \cup {NoSection}]
    /\ clearedTo \in [Trains -> Sections \cup {NoSection}]
    /\ toldOf \in [Signallers -> SUBSET Trains]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [g \in Signallers |-> NoStamp]
    /\ berthed = [t \in Trains |-> NoSection]
    /\ clearedTo = [t \in Trains |-> NoSection]
    /\ toldOf = [g \in Signallers |-> {}]

ReadPlan(g) ==
    /\ snap[g] = NoStamp
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![g] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, berthed, clearedTo, toldOf >>

\* Position reports surface in whatever order the trackside network delivers.
Report(g, t) ==
    /\ t \notin toldOf[g]
    /\ toldOf' = [toldOf EXCEPT ![g] = @ \cup {t}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, berthed, clearedTo >>

Clear(g, t, sec) ==
    /\ snap[g] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ t \in toldOf[g]
    /\ berthed[t] = NoSection
    /\ clearedTo[t] = NoSection
    /\ Occupancy(sec) < SectionLimit
    /\ clearedTo' = [clearedTo EXCEPT ![t] = sec]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![g] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << berthed, toldOf >>

Retry(g) ==
    /\ snap[g] # NoStamp
    /\ snap[g] # version
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![g] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, berthed, clearedTo, toldOf >>

Abandon(g) ==
    /\ snap[g] # NoStamp
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![g] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, berthed, clearedTo, toldOf >>

Arrive(t) ==
    /\ clearedTo[t] # NoSection
    /\ berthed' = [berthed EXCEPT ![t] = clearedTo[t]]
    /\ clearedTo' = [clearedTo EXCEPT ![t] = NoSection]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, toldOf >>

Depart(t) ==
    /\ berthed[t] # NoSection
    /\ berthed' = [berthed EXCEPT ![t] = NoSection]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, snap, clearedTo, toldOf >>

Next ==
    \/ \E g \in Signallers : ReadPlan(g) \/ Retry(g) \/ Abandon(g)
    \/ \E g \in Signallers, t \in Trains : Report(g, t)
    \/ \E g \in Signallers, t \in Trains, sec \in Sections : Clear(g, t, sec)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Arrive(t) \/ Depart(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SectionsWithinTheirLimit ==
    \A sec \in Sections : Occupancy(sec) <= SectionLimit

====
nl:
A subway line is worked in sections, and each section can hold only so many trains at once. Signallers write clearances into one shared occupancy plan without locking it: a signaller reads the plan, taking its version stamp, and its clearance only lands if the stamp is unchanged, otherwise it retries. Train position reports reach the signallers over the trackside network, which promises nothing about order, so a signaller may only clear a train it has actually been told about, and it may be told about trains in any order. A train that has been cleared into a section but has not arrived yet already counts against that section, because the room has to be kept for it.

A signaller holding no snapshot may read the plan, taking its version stamp. A position report for any train may reach any signaller, in any order. A signaller whose snapshot stamp still matches the plan may clear a train it has been told about, and that is neither berthed nor already cleared, into a section, provided that section's berthed trains plus its already-cleared trains are below its limit: the clearance is recorded, the plan's version stamp advances, and the snapshot is closed. A signaller whose snapshot stamp no longer matches the plan retries. A signaller may also simply abandon a snapshot it is holding and read again later. A train that has been cleared may arrive, taking its berth in the section. A berthed train may depart the section.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every section, the trains berthed in it plus the trains cleared into it but not yet arrived never exceed that section's limit.

---- MODULE W4Od8m5p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, Students, MaxEpoch, MaxLimit, NoServer

\* servedBy points from the student to the server holding their session; the
\* safety property reads the server's epoch through that pointer.
VARIABLES epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, state, limit

vars == << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, state, limit >>

Current(s) == srvEpoch[s] = epoch
Backers(s) == {k \in Servers : endorse[k] = s}
Entitled(s) == Current(s) /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(s)) > Cardinality(Servers)
OpenSessions == Cardinality({st \in Students : servedBy[st] # NoServer})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ srvEpoch \in [Servers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ endorse \in [Servers -> Servers \cup {NoServer}]
    /\ servedBy \in [Students -> Servers \cup {NoServer}]
    /\ state \in [Students -> {"waiting", "enrolled", "turned"}]
    /\ limit \in 0..MaxLimit

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ srvEpoch = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ endorse = [s \in Servers |-> NoServer]
    /\ servedBy = [st \in Students |-> NoServer]
    /\ state = [st \in Students |-> "waiting"]
    /\ limit = 1

Resync(s) ==
    /\ ~Current(s)
    /\ srvEpoch' = [srvEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, endorse, servedBy, state, limit >>

Endorse(k, s) ==
    /\ Current(k)
    /\ Current(s)
    /\ endorse[k] # s
    /\ endorse' = [endorse EXCEPT ![k] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, servedBy, state, limit >>

OpenSession(s, st) ==
    /\ Entitled(s)
    /\ state[st] = "waiting"
    /\ servedBy[st] = NoServer
    /\ OpenSessions < limit
    /\ servedBy' = [servedBy EXCEPT ![st] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, state, limit >>

Enrol(st) ==
    /\ servedBy[st] # NoServer
    /\ state[st] = "waiting"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![st] = "enrolled"]
    /\ servedBy' = [servedBy EXCEPT ![st] = NoServer]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, limit >>

\* A student is turned away when the registry is full, and also when no server
\* is entitled to serve anyone at all -- a split endorsement is not a reason to
\* leave someone queued for ever.
TurnAway(st) ==
    /\ state[st] = "waiting"
    /\ servedBy[st] = NoServer
    /\ \/ OpenSessions >= limit
       \/ \A s \in Servers : ~Entitled(s)
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![st] = "turned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, limit >>

\* Reconfiguration voids standing and drops every session, because the server
\* holding one may no longer be entitled to it.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ endorse' = [k \in Servers |-> NoServer]
    /\ servedBy' = [st \in Students |-> NoServer]
    /\ UNCHANGED << srvEpoch, state, limit >>

SetLimit(l) ==
    /\ l # limit
    /\ l >= OpenSessions
    /\ limit' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, state >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Resync(s)
    \/ \E k \in Servers, s \in Servers : Endorse(k, s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, st \in Students : OpenSession(s, st)
    \/ \E st \in Students : Enrol(st) \/ TurnAway(st)
    \/ \E l \in 0..MaxLimit : SetLimit(l)
    \/ Reconfigure

\* Sessions and turn-aways both flicker with the epoch and the limit, so each
\* student needs strong fairness on getting served and on being turned away.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A st \in Students :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E s \in Servers : OpenSession(s, st))
        /\ SF_vars(Enrol(st))
        /\ SF_vars(TurnAway(st))
    /\ \A s \in Servers :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Resync(s))

SessionsAreHeldByCurrentServers ==
    \A st \in Students : servedBy[st] # NoServer => srvEpoch[servedBy[st]] = epoch

EveryWaitingStudentSettles ==
    \A st \in Students : (state[st] = "waiting") ~> (state[st] \in {"enrolled", "turned"})

====

CONSTANTS
    Servers = {regA, regB, regC}
    Students = {stu1, stu2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxLimit = 2
    NoServer = noServer

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SessionsAreHeldByCurrentServers

PROPERTY EveryWaitingStudentSettles
nl:
A university runs course registration through a set of registry servers. The registry is reconfigured whenever the enrolment rules change, which advances its rule epoch and voids every server's standing: a server may only act on a student's behalf while it has resynchronised to the current epoch and a strict majority of the servers endorse it for that epoch. Reconfiguration also drops every registration session in progress, because the server holding it may no longer be entitled to hold it. How many sessions the registry will carry at once is a runtime setting the registrar raises and lowers as load moves, never below the sessions already open.

A server whose epoch is behind the registry's may resynchronise to it. A server that has resynchronised may endorse any resynchronised server for the current epoch, replacing whatever endorsement it was carrying. A resynchronised server endorsed by a strict majority may open a session for a waiting student, provided the sessions already open are below the current setting. A server holding a session may enrol its student, closing the session. A waiting student may be turned away when the sessions already open have reached the setting, and also when no server at all is entitled to act, since a split endorsement is not a reason to leave someone queued indefinitely. The registry may reconfigure while it has rule changes left in its schedule, which advances the epoch, clears every endorsement, and drops every open session back to waiting. The registrar may set the session limit to any different value that is not below the sessions currently open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every student with a registration session open is being served by a server that has resynchronised to the registry's current rule epoch.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every waiting student is eventually either enrolled or turned away.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS MainSite, Annexe, Cases, MaxVersion, NoCase, NoStamp

Planners == MainSite \cup Annexe
Systems == {"main", "annexe"}

\* Which of the two separately installed systems a planner belongs to.
SystemOf(p) == IF p \in MainSite THEN "main" ELSE "annexe"

vars == << version, plan, snapStamp, snapSet, choice, confirmed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ plan \in SUBSET Cases
    /\ snapStamp \in [Planners -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ snapSet \in [Planners -> SUBSET Cases]
    /\ choice \in [Planners -> Cases \cup {NoCase}]
    /\ confirmed \in [Systems -> SUBSET Cases]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ plan = {}
    /\ snapStamp = [p \in Planners |-> NoStamp]
    /\ snapSet = [p \in Planners |-> {}]
    /\ choice = [p \in Planners |-> NoCase]
    /\ confirmed = [k \in Systems |-> {}]

ReadPlan(p) ==
    /\ snapStamp[p] = NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = plan]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, choice, confirmed >>

Choose(p, c) ==
    /\ snapStamp[p] # NoStamp
    /\ choice[p] = NoCase
    /\ c \notin snapSet[p]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, snapStamp, snapSet, confirmed >>

\* The write-back carries the planner's own copy of the plan, so committing on
\* a stamp that has moved would erase whatever the other system confirmed.
Confirm(p) ==
    /\ snapStamp[p] = version
    /\ choice[p] # NoCase
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ plan' = snapSet[p] \cup {choice[p]}
    /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![SystemOf(p)] = @ \cup {choice[p]}]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![p] = NoStamp]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoCase]

Retry(p) ==
    /\ snapStamp[p] # NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp[p] # version
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![p] = NoStamp]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoCase]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, confirmed >>

Abandon(p) ==
    /\ snapStamp[p] # NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![p] = NoStamp]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoCase]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, confirmed >>

DropChoice(p) ==
    /\ choice[p] # NoCase
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoCase]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, snapStamp, snapSet, confirmed >>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Planners : ReadPlan(p) \/ Confirm(p) \/ Retry(p) \/ DropChoice(p) \/ Abandon(p)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, c \in Cases : Choose(p, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BothSystemsConfirmationsStillStand ==
    \A k \in Systems : confirmed[k] \subseteq plan

====
nl:
A hospital merged with a neighbouring trust and now runs two theatre scheduling systems, the main-site one and the annexe one, each installed as though it were the only one. Both write the same shared theatre day plan: the set of cases accepted for the day. Neither system locks the plan. A planner reads it, taking both its version stamp and a copy of its case set, and writes back only if the stamp is unchanged, retrying otherwise. Each system also keeps its own confirmation list -- the cases it has told its surgeons are going ahead -- and a case on a confirmation list that has fallen out of the shared plan is a theatre slot the hospital thinks it has and does not.

A planner holding no snapshot may read the plan, taking its stamp and a copy of the case set. A planner holding a snapshot but no chosen case may choose a case that is not already in its snapshot. A planner holding a snapshot and a chosen case may confirm it if the plan's stamp still matches what it read: the plan becomes that planner's snapshot plus the chosen case, the case joins that planner's own system's confirmation list, the stamp advances, and the snapshot and choice are cleared. A planner whose stamp no longer matches the plan retries, discarding its snapshot and its choice. A planner may drop its chosen case while keeping its snapshot, and may abandon a snapshot entirely and read again later.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every case on either system's confirmation list is still in the shared theatre day plan.
