---- MODULE W4Od18m1p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS OldHub, NewHub, OldGuests, NewGuests, Slots, NoGuest, NoSlot

\* Two separately fitted hubs, one ring, one pool of slots between them. Each
\* guest is enrolled on one hub, so a guest is only served while the ring token
\* is with a controller of that hub.
Controllers == OldHub \cup NewHub
Guests == OldGuests \cup NewGuests
HubOfGuest(g) == IF g \in OldGuests THEN "old" ELSE "new"
HubOfCtl(c) == IF c \in OldHub THEN "old" ELSE "new"

VARIABLES token, register, keySlot, ask

vars == << token, register, keySlot, ask >>

Serving(g) == HubOfCtl(token) = HubOfGuest(g)

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Controllers
    /\ register \in [Slots -> Guests \cup {NoGuest}]
    /\ keySlot \in [Guests -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ ask \in [Guests -> {"idle", "waiting", "holding", "turned"}]

Init ==
    /\ token = CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE
    /\ register = [s \in Slots |-> NoGuest]
    /\ keySlot = [g \in Guests |-> NoSlot]
    /\ ask = [g \in Guests |-> "waiting"]

PassToken(c) ==
    /\ c # token
    /\ token' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED << register, keySlot, ask >>

\* Only the token holder allocates, and both records are written together.
Allocate(g, s) ==
    /\ Serving(g)
    /\ ask[g] = "waiting"
    /\ register[s] = NoGuest
    /\ keySlot[g] = NoSlot
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ keySlot' = [keySlot EXCEPT ![g] = s]
    /\ ask' = [ask EXCEPT ![g] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token >>

TurnAway(g) ==
    /\ Serving(g)
    /\ ask[g] = "waiting"
    /\ \A s \in Slots : register[s] # NoGuest
    /\ ask' = [ask EXCEPT ![g] = "turned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, register, keySlot >>

GiveBack(g) ==
    /\ ask[g] = "holding"
    /\ keySlot[g] # NoSlot
    /\ register' = [s \in Slots |-> IF register[s] = g THEN NoGuest ELSE register[s]]
    /\ keySlot' = [keySlot EXCEPT ![g] = NoSlot]
    /\ ask' = [ask EXCEPT ![g] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token >>

AskAgain(g) ==
    /\ ask[g] \in {"idle", "turned"}
    /\ ask' = [ask EXCEPT ![g] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, register, keySlot >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : PassToken(c)
    \/ \E g \in Guests, s \in Slots : Allocate(g, s)
    \/ \E g \in Guests : TurnAway(g) \/ GiveBack(g) \/ AskAgain(g)

\* The token has to come round to a guest's own hub before anything can happen
\* for that guest, so both decisions need strong fairness and the ring itself
\* has to keep turning.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A g \in Guests :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E s \in Slots : Allocate(g, s))
        /\ SF_vars(TurnAway(g))
    /\ \A c \in Controllers :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(PassToken(c))

RegisterAndKeysAgree ==
    \A s \in Slots : register[s] # NoGuest => keySlot[register[s]] = s

EveryAskIsSettled ==
    \A g \in Guests : (ask[g] = "waiting") ~> (ask[g] \in {"holding", "turned"})

====
nl:
A household ended up with two door-lock hubs, the original one and the one the alarm company fitted later, and both hand out the same pool of guest access slots. To stop them handing out the same slot twice they share a ring token: the hubs' controllers pass a single token round a ring, and only the controller holding it may allocate. The pool keeps one register saying which guest holds each slot, and each guest key records the slot it was given, so the two records have to agree in both directions.

Every guest is enrolled on one of the two hubs, and a guest is only ever served while the ring token happens to be with a controller of that guest's own hub. A guest may ask for a slot. A controller holding the token may allocate a free slot to a waiting guest enrolled on its own hub: the register records the guest against the slot and the guest's key records the slot. A controller holding the token may turn away a waiting guest of its own hub when no slot in the register is free. A guest holding a slot may give it back, clearing both records. The token holder may pass the token to any other controller in the ring. A guest that was turned away may ask again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every slot the register has allocated, the guest named in the register records that same slot, so the two hubs never hand one slot to two guests.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every guest who has asked for a slot is eventually either given one or turned away.

---- MODULE W4Od3m9p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Banks, ChannelLimit, MaxEpoch, MaxClosures, NoBank

\* A half-open channel has already reserved the counterparty's line, so both
\* terms below count against that counterparty's limit.
VARIABLES epoch, nodeEpoch, opening, open, closures

vars == << epoch, nodeEpoch, opening, open, closures >>

Committed(b) ==
    Cardinality({n \in Nodes : open[n] = b})
      + Cardinality({n \in Nodes : opening[n] = b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ nodeEpoch \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ opening \in [Nodes -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]
    /\ open \in [Nodes -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]
    /\ closures \in 0..MaxClosures

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ nodeEpoch = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ opening = [n \in Nodes |-> NoBank]
    /\ open = [n \in Nodes |-> NoBank]
    /\ closures = 0

Resync(n) ==
    /\ nodeEpoch[n] # epoch
    /\ nodeEpoch' = [nodeEpoch EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, opening, open, closures >>

BeginOpen(n, b) ==
    /\ nodeEpoch[n] = epoch
    /\ opening[n] = NoBank
    /\ open[n] = NoBank
    /\ Committed(b) < ChannelLimit
    /\ opening' = [opening EXCEPT ![n] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, nodeEpoch, open, closures >>

CompleteOpen(n) ==
    /\ opening[n] # NoBank
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![n] = opening[n]]
    /\ opening' = [opening EXCEPT ![n] = NoBank]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, nodeEpoch, closures >>

Close(n) ==
    /\ open[n] # NoBank
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![n] = NoBank]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, nodeEpoch, opening, closures >>

\* The desk's closure takes down whichever half of the channel exists.
ForceClose(n) ==
    /\ closures < MaxClosures
    /\ opening[n] # NoBank \/ open[n] # NoBank
    /\ opening' = [opening EXCEPT ![n] = NoBank]
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![n] = NoBank]
    /\ closures' = closures + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, nodeEpoch >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << nodeEpoch, opening, open, closures >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Resync(n) \/ CompleteOpen(n) \/ Close(n) \/ ForceClose(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, b \in Banks : BeginOpen(n, b)
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CounterpartyChannelsWithinLimit ==
    \A b \in Banks : Committed(b) <= ChannelLimit

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {setA, setB, setC}
    Banks = {cptyX, cptyY}
    ChannelLimit = 1
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxClosures = 1
    NoBank = noBank

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CounterpartyChannelsWithinLimit
nl:
A clearing house opens settlement channels from its settlement nodes to each counterparty bank. A counterparty will only accept so many channels at once, and a channel that a node has begun opening but not yet completed already counts against that counterparty, because the counterparty has reserved the line for it. The service runs in numbered configurations: reconfiguration advances the epoch and every node must resynchronise before it may begin opening anything. The treasury desk holds a bounded number of privileged closures for channels that must be torn down without waiting for the node that owns them.

A node whose epoch is behind the service's may resynchronise. A node that has resynchronised, and that has no channel of its own, may begin opening a channel to a counterparty, provided that counterparty's channels already open plus those already being opened are below its limit. A node that is opening a channel may complete it. A node with an open channel may close it. The treasury desk may force any node's channel closed, whether it is open or still opening, spending one privileged closure. The service may reconfigure while it has configurations left in its schedule, which advances the epoch; channels already open or opening are not disturbed by it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every counterparty bank, the channels open to it plus the channels being opened to it never exceed that counterparty's channel limit.

---- MODULE W4Od12m6p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Orders, StorageSlots, MaxGen, LeaseTicks, MaxLimit, NoSlot

\* Granting a slot advances its generation, so an order still pointing at a
\* slot under an older stamp is exactly what the invariant rules out.
VARIABLES heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, ttl, limit

vars == << heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, ttl, limit >>

OnLease == Cardinality({o \in Orders : heldSlot[o] # NoSlot})

TypeOK ==
    /\ heldSlot \in [Orders -> StorageSlots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ leaseGen \in [Orders -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ slotGen \in [StorageSlots -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ ttl \in [Orders -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ limit \in 0..MaxLimit

Init ==
    /\ heldSlot = [o \in Orders |-> NoSlot]
    /\ leaseGen = [o \in Orders |-> 0]
    /\ slotGen = [s \in StorageSlots |-> 0]
    /\ ttl = [o \in Orders |-> 0]
    /\ limit = 1

Grant(o, s) ==
    /\ heldSlot[o] = NoSlot
    /\ \A p \in Orders : heldSlot[p] # s
    /\ slotGen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ OnLease < limit
    /\ slotGen' = [slotGen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ leaseGen' = [leaseGen EXCEPT ![o] = slotGen[s] + 1]
    /\ heldSlot' = [heldSlot EXCEPT ![o] = s]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![o] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED << limit >>

\* The clock runs every live lease down together.
Tick ==
    /\ \E o \in Orders : heldSlot[o] # NoSlot /\ ttl[o] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [o \in Orders |->
                 IF heldSlot[o] # NoSlot /\ ttl[o] > 0 THEN ttl[o] - 1 ELSE ttl[o]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, limit >>

Reclaim(o) ==
    /\ heldSlot[o] # NoSlot
    /\ ttl[o] = 0
    /\ heldSlot' = [heldSlot EXCEPT ![o] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leaseGen, slotGen, ttl, limit >>

Complete(o) ==
    /\ heldSlot[o] # NoSlot
    /\ heldSlot' = [heldSlot EXCEPT ![o] = NoSlot]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leaseGen, slotGen, limit >>

SetLimit(l) ==
    /\ l # limit
    /\ l >= OnLease
    /\ limit' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED << heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, ttl >>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in StorageSlots : Grant(o, s)
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Reclaim(o) \/ Complete(o)
    \/ \E l \in 0..MaxLimit : SetLimit(l)
    \/ Tick

\* Completing is never blocked, so weak fairness per order is enough to see
\* every lease given back.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A o \in Orders :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Complete(o))

LeasesCarryTheirSlotsGeneration ==
    \A o \in Orders : heldSlot[o] # NoSlot => leaseGen[o] = slotGen[heldSlot[o]]

EveryLeaseIsGivenBack ==
    \A o \in Orders : (heldSlot[o] # NoSlot) ~> (heldSlot[o] = NoSlot)

====

CONSTANTS
    Orders = {ordA, ordB}
    StorageSlots = {binA, binB}
    MaxGen = 2
    LeaseTicks = 2
    MaxLimit = 2
    NoSlot = noSlot

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LeasesCarryTheirSlotsGeneration

PROPERTY EveryLeaseIsGivenBack
nl:
A blood bank holds product in numbered storage slots and leases a slot to an order while that order is being made up. A lease is not permanent: it carries a countdown and lapses if the order is not completed in time. Every slot carries a lease generation, and a lease handed to an order is stamped with the generation the slot had when it was granted; granting a slot advances its generation, so any older lease on it is dead paper. How many slots the bank will have out on lease at once is a runtime setting the duty manager raises and lowers as the fridge fills, never below the leases already out.

The bank may grant a slot to an order that holds none, provided the slot is held by nobody, and provided the leases already out are below the current setting: the slot's generation advances, the order's lease is stamped with that new generation, and the countdown starts full. The bank's clock may tick while at least one lease still has countdown left, running down every live lease at once. A lease whose countdown has reached zero may be reclaimed, which takes the slot back from the order. An order holding a slot may complete, releasing the slot. The duty manager may set the lease limit to any different value that is not below the leases currently out.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every order holding a slot holds it under a lease stamped with that slot's current generation, so a slot handed on to a new order leaves no older holder behind.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order that has been granted a slot eventually stops holding it.

---- MODULE W4Od4m1p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS OldSystem, NewSystem, Stages, Settings, NoSetting

\* Two separately installed control systems, one ring, one programme record.
Controllers == OldSystem \cup NewSystem
Systems == {"old", "new"}
SystemOf(c) == IF c \in OldSystem THEN "old" ELSE "new"

VARIABLES token, record, acked, prepared

vars == << token, record, acked, prepared >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Controllers
    /\ record \in [Stages -> Settings \cup {NoSetting}]
    /\ acked \in [Systems -> [Stages -> Settings \cup {NoSetting}]]
    /\ prepared \in [Controllers -> Settings \cup {NoSetting}]

Init ==
    /\ token = CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE
    /\ record = [st \in Stages |-> NoSetting]
    /\ acked = [k \in Systems |-> [st \in Stages |-> NoSetting]]
    /\ prepared = [c \in Controllers |-> NoSetting]

PassToken(c) ==
    /\ c # token
    /\ token' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED << record, acked, prepared >>

Prepare(c, v) ==
    /\ prepared[c] # v
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![c] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, record, acked >>

\* Writing strikes the stage from both acknowledged copies: whatever the
\* operators were told about this stage is no longer good.
Write(c, st) ==
    /\ c = token
    /\ prepared[c] # NoSetting
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![st] = prepared[c]]
    /\ acked' = [k \in Systems |-> [acked[k] EXCEPT ![st] = NoSetting]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, prepared >>

Acknowledge(k, st) ==
    /\ acked[k][st] # record[st]
    /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![k][st] = record[st]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, record, prepared >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : PassToken(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, v \in Settings : Prepare(c, v)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, st \in Stages : Write(c, st)
    \/ \E k \in Systems, st \in Stages : Acknowledge(k, st)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AcknowledgedSettingsStillHold ==
    \A k \in Systems, st \in Stages :
        acked[k][st] # NoSetting => record[st] = acked[k][st]

====
nl:
A car wash was rebuilt around an older wash controller that was never removed, so two control systems now drive the same conveyor and share one programme record: the setting in force at each stage of the wash. Only one of them may write at a time, and that is arranged with a ring token passed between the systems' controllers. Each system also keeps its own acknowledged copy -- the settings it has told its operators are in force -- and an acknowledged setting that no longer matches the record is an operator running the wash on a setting that was overwritten. A write therefore strikes that stage from both systems' acknowledged copies, so a setting has to be acknowledged afresh before anyone relies on it.

The token holder may pass the token to any other controller in the ring. A controller may prepare a setting it intends to write, replacing whatever it was preparing. The controller holding the token, with a setting prepared, may write it to a stage: the record takes the setting and that stage is struck from every system's acknowledged copy. A system may acknowledge a stage whose record setting is not what it has acknowledged, taking the record's current setting into its own copy.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Wherever a system has acknowledged a setting for a wash stage, the shared programme record still holds that same setting for that stage.

---- MODULE W4Od12m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, Fridges, MaxCapacity, LeaseTicks, NoFridge

\* A lease holds space that no unit occupies yet, so both terms below count
\* against the refrigerator's capacity.
VARIABLES stored, leased, ttl, capacity

vars == << stored, leased, ttl, capacity >>

Committed(f) ==
    Cardinality({u \in Units : stored[u] = f})
      + Cardinality({u \in Units : leased[u] = f})

TypeOK ==
    /\ stored \in [Units -> Fridges \cup {NoFridge}]
    /\ leased \in [Units -> Fridges \cup {NoFridge}]
    /\ ttl \in [Units -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ capacity \in [Fridges -> 0..MaxCapacity]

Init ==
    /\ stored = [u \in Units |-> NoFridge]
    /\ leased = [u \in Units |-> NoFridge]
    /\ ttl = [u \in Units |-> 0]
    /\ capacity = [f \in Fridges |-> 1]

TakeLease(u, f) ==
    /\ stored[u] = NoFridge
    /\ leased[u] = NoFridge
    /\ Committed(f) < capacity[f]
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![u] = f]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stored, capacity >>

\* One clock runs every outstanding lease down together.
Tick ==
    /\ \E u \in Units : leased[u] # NoFridge /\ ttl[u] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [u \in Units |->
                 IF leased[u] # NoFridge /\ ttl[u] > 0 THEN ttl[u] - 1 ELSE ttl[u]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stored, leased, capacity >>

Reclaim(u) ==
    /\ leased[u] # NoFridge
    /\ ttl[u] = 0
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![u] = NoFridge]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stored, ttl, capacity >>

PutAway(u) ==
    /\ leased[u] # NoFridge
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![u] = leased[u]]
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![u] = NoFridge]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED << capacity >>

Issue(u) ==
    /\ stored[u] # NoFridge
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![u] = NoFridge]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leased, ttl, capacity >>

SetCapacity(f, c) ==
    /\ c # capacity[f]
    /\ c >= Committed(f)
    /\ capacity' = [capacity EXCEPT ![f] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stored, leased, ttl >>

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Units, f \in Fridges : TakeLease(u, f)
    \/ \E u \in Units : Reclaim(u) \/ PutAway(u) \/ Issue(u)
    \/ \E f \in Fridges, c \in 0..MaxCapacity : SetCapacity(f, c)
    \/ Tick

\* Putting a unit away is never blocked, so weak fairness per unit closes out
\* every lease one way or the other.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A u \in Units :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(PutAway(u))

FridgesWithinCapacity == \A f \in Fridges : Committed(f) <= capacity[f]

EveryLeaseIsResolved ==
    \A u \in Units : (leased[u] # NoFridge) ~> (leased[u] = NoFridge)

====

CONSTANTS
    Units = {unitA, unitB}
    Fridges = {frgN, frgS}
    MaxCapacity = 2
    LeaseTicks = 2
    NoFridge = noFridge

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FridgesWithinCapacity

PROPERTY EveryLeaseIsResolved
nl:
A blood bank stores units in refrigerators of bounded capacity. Before a unit can be put away, space for it is leased in a particular refrigerator, and that lease counts against the refrigerator's capacity from the moment it is taken, not from the moment the unit arrives -- the space has to be kept. Leases expire: each carries a countdown, and a lease that runs out is reclaimed and the space goes back. Each refrigerator's capacity is a runtime setting: the estates team raises and lowers it as compressors are serviced, never below what that refrigerator is already committed to.

A unit that is neither stored nor holding a lease may take a lease on a refrigerator, provided that refrigerator's stored units plus its outstanding leases are below its current capacity; the countdown starts full. The bank's clock may tick while at least one lease still has countdown left, running down every outstanding lease at once. A lease whose countdown has reached zero may be reclaimed, freeing the space again. A unit holding a lease may be put away into that refrigerator, which turns the lease into stored product. A stored unit may be issued out of the refrigerator. The estates team may set a refrigerator's capacity to any different value that is not below its stored units plus its outstanding leases.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every refrigerator, its stored units plus its outstanding space leases never exceed that refrigerator's current capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every unit holding a space lease eventually stops holding it.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Signallers, Routes, Free, NoRoute, NoRead, NoSignaller

\* readOn/readVal are the signaller's outstanding read of a route register; the
\* set only lands if the register still agrees with what was read.
VARIABLES reg, readOn, readVal, withdrawn, offPanel

vars == << reg, readOn, readVal, withdrawn, offPanel >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Routes -> Signallers \cup {Free}]
    /\ readOn \in [Signallers -> Routes \cup {NoRoute}]
    /\ readVal \in [Signallers -> Signallers \cup {Free, NoRead}]
    /\ withdrawn \in SUBSET Signallers
    /\ offPanel \in Signallers \cup {NoSignaller}

Init ==
    /\ reg = [r \in Routes |-> Free]
    /\ readOn = [s \in Signallers |-> NoRoute]
    /\ readVal = [s \in Signallers |-> NoRead]
    /\ withdrawn = {}
    /\ offPanel = NoSignaller

ReadRoute(s, r) ==
    /\ s # offPanel
    /\ readOn[s] = NoRoute
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![s] = reg[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, withdrawn, offPanel >>

\* The compare half, plus the authority test, both taken at the moment the
\* route is set.
SetRoute(s) ==
    /\ s # offPanel
    /\ s \notin withdrawn
    /\ readOn[s] # NoRoute
    /\ readVal[s] = Free
    /\ reg[readOn[s]] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![readOn[s]] = s]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoRoute]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![s] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << withdrawn, offPanel >>

StaleRead(s) ==
    /\ readOn[s] # NoRoute
    /\ readVal[s] # reg[readOn[s]]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoRoute]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![s] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, withdrawn, offPanel >>

GiveUpRoute(s, r) ==
    /\ reg[r] = s
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED << readOn, readVal, withdrawn, offPanel >>

\* Withdrawal has to reach the signaller, so it can only be applied to one on
\* the panel, and it gives up that signaller's routes in the same movement.
Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ s \notin withdrawn
    /\ s # offPanel
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn \cup {s}
    /\ reg' = [r \in Routes |-> IF reg[r] = s THEN Free ELSE reg[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << readOn, readVal, offPanel >>

Restore(s) ==
    /\ s \in withdrawn
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, readOn, readVal, offPanel >>

StepOff(s) == /\ offPanel = NoSignaller /\ offPanel' = s /\ UNCHANGED << reg, readOn, readVal, withdrawn >>
StepOn     == /\ offPanel # NoSignaller /\ offPanel' = NoSignaller /\ UNCHANGED << reg, readOn, readVal, withdrawn >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Signallers, r \in Routes : ReadRoute(s, r) \/ GiveUpRoute(s, r)
    \/ \E s \in Signallers : SetRoute(s) \/ StaleRead(s) \/ Withdraw(s) \/ Restore(s) \/ StepOff(s)
    \/ StepOn

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoRouteHeldByAWithdrawnSignaller ==
    \A r \in Routes : reg[r] # Free => reg[r] \notin withdrawn

nl:
A subway interlocking lets signallers set routes through the junction. Each route has a register in the interlocking that either reads free or names the signaller that set it, and signallers take routes by compare-and-swap: a signaller reads a route's register, then writes its own name in only if the register still reads what it read. Setting a route is an authorised act, and the control centre withdraws a signaller's authority when a panel is handed over or a rating lapses. Signallers are slow rather than failed: at most one at a time is off the panel, and always comes back -- and the control centre will not withdraw authority from a signaller it cannot reach, because withdrawal has to give up that signaller's routes at the same moment.

A signaller on the panel holding no outstanding read may read any route's register, remembering the route and what it saw. A signaller on the panel whose read still matches that route's register, whose read said the route was free, and who has authority, may set the route: the register takes its name and the read is cleared. A signaller whose remembered value no longer matches the register discards the read. A signaller may give up a route its name is on. The control centre may withdraw authority from a signaller it can reach, which strikes that signaller's name off every route it holds in the same movement, and may restore authority to a signaller that has none. Finally, the one signaller on the panel may step off, and the signaller who stepped off may come back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No route is ever left set in the name of a signaller whose authority has been withdrawn.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Instructions, Bays, MaxTerm, NoCtl, NoInstr, NoBay

\* ackedAt[u] is the bay the shipping line was told about; it must never name
\* a bay the plan has moved on from.
VARIABLES term, backing, chair, plan, ackedAt

vars == << term, backing, chair, plan, ackedAt >>

Backers(n) == {k \in Controllers : backing[k] = n}
Placed(u) == \E b \in Bays : plan[b] = u

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ backing \in [Controllers -> Controllers \cup {NoCtl}]
    /\ chair \in Controllers \cup {NoCtl}
    /\ plan \in [Bays -> Instructions \cup {NoInstr}]
    /\ ackedAt \in [Instructions -> Bays \cup {NoBay}]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ backing = [k \in Controllers |-> NoCtl]
    /\ chair = NoCtl
    /\ plan = [b \in Bays |-> NoInstr]
    /\ ackedAt = [u \in Instructions |-> NoBay]

Back(k, n) ==
    /\ backing[k] # n
    /\ backing' = [backing EXCEPT ![k] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, chair, plan, ackedAt >>

TakeChair(n) ==
    /\ chair = NoCtl
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(n)) > Cardinality(Controllers)
    /\ chair' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, plan, ackedAt >>

Write(u, b) ==
    /\ chair # NoCtl
    /\ plan[b] = NoInstr
    /\ ~Placed(u)
    /\ ackedAt[u] = NoBay
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![b] = u]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, ackedAt >>

\* Acknowledgements land in any order at all.
Acknowledge(u, b) ==
    /\ plan[b] = u
    /\ ackedAt[u] = NoBay
    /\ ackedAt' = [ackedAt EXCEPT ![u] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, plan >>

\* Clearing a bay withdraws the acknowledgement in the same movement; that is
\* the whole of the property.
Clear(u) ==
    /\ chair # NoCtl
    /\ ackedAt[u] # NoBay
    /\ plan' = [b \in Bays |-> IF plan[b] = u THEN NoInstr ELSE plan[b]]
    /\ ackedAt' = [ackedAt EXCEPT ![u] = NoBay]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair >>

\* A failover empties the chair and voids the backings; the plan and the
\* acknowledgements survive it untouched.
FailOver ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ chair' = NoCtl
    /\ backing' = [k \in Controllers |-> NoCtl]
    /\ UNCHANGED << plan, ackedAt >>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Controllers, n \in Controllers : Back(k, n)
    \/ \E n \in Controllers : TakeChair(n)
    \/ \E u \in Instructions, b \in Bays : Write(u, b) \/ Acknowledge(u, b)
    \/ \E u \in Instructions : Clear(u)
    \/ FailOver

\* Acknowledging does not wait on the chair, so weak fairness per instruction
\* is enough to see every placed instruction acknowledged.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A u \in Instructions :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bays : Acknowledge(u, b))

AcknowledgedInstructionsStillSitInTheirBays ==
    \A u \in Instructions : ackedAt[u] # NoBay => plan[ackedAt[u]] = u

EveryPlacedInstructionIsAcknowledged ==
    \A u \in Instructions : Placed(u) ~> (ackedAt[u] # NoBay)

nl:
A container terminal keeps one stow plan: which loading instruction occupies each bay of the ship. The plan is written only by the elected yard master, and the yard master's chair fails over to another controller when the sitting one is thought to have gone. Once an instruction is in a bay, the terminal acknowledges it back to the shipping line, and that acknowledgement is what the line plans its cargo around. Acknowledgements travel over the terminal's message fabric, which promises nothing about order, so they land in whatever order they land. The one thing the terminal must never do is clear an acknowledged instruction out from under the line without withdrawing the acknowledgement in the same movement.

A controller may back any controller it is not already backing. A controller backed by a strict majority may take the yard master's chair when the chair is empty. The sitting yard master may write an instruction that is not already in the plan into an empty bay. An instruction sitting in a bay that has not been acknowledged may be acknowledged, in any order relative to any other acknowledgement, recording the bay the line was told about. The sitting yard master may clear an acknowledged instruction out of its bay, which withdraws the acknowledgement at the same time. The chair may fail over while there are terms left in the schedule: the term advances, the chair empties, and every backing is cleared; the plan and the acknowledgements are untouched by it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every instruction the terminal has acknowledged to the shipping line is still sitting in the bay it was acknowledged for.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instruction that has been written into a bay is eventually acknowledged to the shipping line.
